summary: Grandson of Bull Smith who held land near Hauppauge in the 1736 division of Smithtown and settled at Moriches; John's 8th-great-grandfather.
bio:
James Smith was born at Smithtown in 1688 or soon after, the son of Job Smith and Elizabeth Thompson and a grandson of Bull Smith. He was once shown as a son of Justice Adam Smith, but Adam's will of 1704 left everything to "his only son Edmund Smith", so that link is wrong. James was living in Smithtown in the mid-1720s, when his earmark was recorded, and in the General Division of 1736 he drew 152 acres "on the east side of Smithtown river, near the northeast branch", bounded on the south by land laid out to Daniel Smith; a tract of his cousin Daniel Smith 2d at the head of the Northeast Branch was in turn bounded on the north by James's land. This is the closest John's direct line comes to the Hauppauge estate. James then sold his shares to his brothers and settled at Moriches on the south shore of Brookhaven.

About 1720 he married Jerusha Topping, daughter of Elnathan and Mary Topping. Their children were Matthew, born 3 September 1721, Ezekiel, Zebulon, Austin, Nathaniel, Francis, Eunice, Keturah, Temperance and Jeremiah. Three sons, Austin, Francis and Jeremiah, moved to Orange County, where Austin and Francis became captains and Jeremiah left a will. A James Smith also petitioned in 1721 for 2,000 acres of the annulled Evans grant in Ulster, now Orange, County, and a survey followed in 1722; if this was the same man, the family's interest in the Highlands began a generation before Austin, Francis and Temperance moved to Woodbury Clove, but that identification is not certain, and the land was apparently never settled.

James died in 1740. He is John's 8th-great-grandfather, and he should not be confused with the later James Smith of Hauppauge, of the Lake Ronkonkoma family, who married Catherine Blydenburgh and died in 1837 aged 95.

researchNotes:
Son of Job Smith 1st & Elizabeth Thompson. In Smithtown in the mid-1720s; his earmark was recorded in 1725 (Pelletreau pp. 82–83). In the 1736 General Division he drew 152 acres 'on the east side of Smithtown river, near the northeast branch,' bounded south by land laid out to Daniel Smith (pp. 311–312); a tract of his first cousin Daniel Smith 2d's 'at the head of the Northeast Branch, bounded south by Islip line' was bounded north 'by James Smith's land' (p. 361) — the closest John's direct line comes to Hauppauge. He then sold shares to his brothers (pp. 297, 398–400) and 'settled in Moriches' on the Brookhaven south shore (App. p. 479). Married Jerusha Topping, daughter of Elnathan & Mary Topping. Children per Pelletreau: Matthew (b. 1721), Ezekiel, Zebulon, Austin, Nathaniel, Francis, Eunice, Keturah, Temperance, Jeremiah. Sons Austin, Francis and Jeremiah went to Orange County (Capts. Austin and Francis Smith; Jeremiah Smith's will 1776/1783). No NY will for James (d. 1740) was found; no Smith will in the Smith Wills volume names Temperance. TREE vs PDF: the tree (and an earlier screenshot version of the chart) shows his father as 'Justice, A Smith' / 'Justice Adam Smith 1649–1726'; the uploaded Bull Smith PDF shows Job Smith + Elizabeth Thompson c.1647–c.1719. Preferred: Job (upload overrides tree; F. K. Smith 'James Smith (Job, Richard)'). Do not confuse with the Hauppauge James Smith (d. 1837 aged 95) from Lake Ronkonkoma, who married Catherine Blydenburgh — a different, non-Bull family.

Pelletreau (1898) lists James among Job Smith's children (Job 2d, 'Saint' Richard, Timothy, Aaron, James, Joseph, Elizabeth). He says James 'settled in Moriches' and married Jerusha Topping, and that their eldest child Matthew was born 3 Sept 1721 ([R4-S1]). The 1688 family deed names only four sons of Job (Job, Richard, Joseph, Timothy), which fits James being born in or after 1688 ([R4-S4]). Weygant's Family Record (1897) independently dates the marriage 'about the year 1720' and calls Jerusha a daughter of Elnathan Topping Jr. ([R4-S2]). Weygant also credits James with a 1722 patent for 2,000 acres of the annulled Capt. John Evans grant in Ulster (now Orange) County, which the family apparently never settled. The Calendar of Land Papers confirms a 1721 petition and a 1722 survey for 'James Smith' ([R4-S3]), but nothing in the calendar entry ties that James Smith to Moriches. Treat it as a candidate. If correct, it shows the family's interest in the Highlands a generation before Austin, Francis and Temperance moved to Woodbury Clove.

The tree names James's father as 'Justice Adam Smith (1649-1726)'. Pelletreau prints Adam Smith's will of 12 June 1704, which leaves all his estate to 'his only son Edmund Smith' ([R4-S5]). Adam therefore had no son James, and the tree's link is wrong: James was the son of Job Smith & Elizabeth Thompson.
